screening_decisions.reason: RCT comparing patient decision aids and surgeon preference reports for osteoarthritis. The feedback consisted of patient treatment preferences, not patient-reported outcome measurements (PROMs) of health status. The intervention is decision support rather than routine PROMs feedback to healthcare providers or patients.

RCT in general dental practice where patients completed the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale (MDAS), a PROM. Dentists were randomly allocated to receive the MDAS score (intervention) or not (control). This is a direct comparison of PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback, with patient-reported outcomes (state anxiety) assessed.

RCT in university counselling randomly assigning therapists to receive session-by-session progress feedback from the Outcome Rating Scale (a brief PROM) or no feedback. This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers versus no feedback on therapeutic outcomes.

Stepped-wedge RCT comparing continuous feedback to therapist plus supervisor versus feedback to therapist alone. There is no arm without PROMs feedback; therefore it does not directly compare providing PROMs feedback with not providing such information.

RCT of a standalone web-based self-management application (Oncokompas) that monitors HRQOL/symptoms and gives automated tailored feedback to cancer survivors. It is a digital behavioural intervention without integration into routine clinical encounters or feedback to healthcare providers, falling outside the scope of routine PROMs feedback in clinical practice.
Integrated literature review and narrative synthesis of principles for graphic display of PRO data. It is not a primary randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

RCT of mobile telehealth involving self-monitoring of physiological data (HbA1c, blood pressure) with nurse-initiated feedback. The intervention is a disease-management/telehealth programme focused on clinical monitoring rather than routine feedback of standardized PROMs to healthcare providers or patients.

RCT in oncology randomly assigning patients to HRQL assessment (EORTC QLQ-C30 and HADS) with feedback to physicians, assessment without feedback, or no assessment. The comparison between the feedback arm and the no-assessment/attention-control arms directly tests the effect of providing PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus not providing it, on patient-reported outcomes and communication processes.

RCT in family medicine where patients completed the Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale (PROM). Symptomatically depressed patients were randomized to have their physician informed of results versus control (physician not informed). This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers versus no feedback on diagnosis and treatment outcomes.

Laboratory study of alcohol impairment and performance feedback in DUI offenders. Not a clinical practice trial, not involving PROMs feedback to healthcare providers or patients, and not assessing health outcomes or processes of care relevant to the review.

Cluster RCT in primary care where physicians were randomized to receive reports summarizing patient anxiety symptom levels and functioning status from a waiting-room screening questionnaire (PROM) versus control. This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback on patient outcomes (anxiety, functioning).

Psychometric validation study of the SF-36 administered by post in patients with common clinical conditions. Not an RCT comparing PROMs feedback versus no feedback; it assesses measurement properties only.

RCT of the internet-based intervention 'Featback' comprising psychoeducation plus an automated monitoring-and-feedback system versus waiting list. This is a comprehensive digital therapeutic intervention rather than a trial isolating the effect of routine PROMs feedback in clinical practice. The control receives no intervention, making it impossible to separate PROMs feedback effects from the overall treatment package.

RCT in a hospital-based group practice where patients completed functional disability questionnaires every four months. Experimental physicians received reports summarizing patient responses; control physicians received no report. Direct comparison of PROMs feedback to healthcare providers versus no feedback on functional status outcomes.

RCT of complex symptom perception and peak-flow training interventions in children with asthma. The study combines asthma education, home monitoring, and discrimination training. It is not a trial of routine feedback of standardized PROMs to healthcare providers or patients.
Feasibility RCT of a multimodal supportive care intervention targeting unmet needs. No mention of PROMs feedback as the intervention; the focus is broad supportive care.
Structured review of controlled trials evaluating PROMs impact on routine practice. Not a primary randomised trial.

The provided abstract describes an observational database study of venous thromboembolism risk in immune-mediated diseases, not a trial of PROMs feedback. Regardless of the title, it is not an RCT and does not compare PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

RCT where case coordinators integrated a validated pain assessment battery and depression scale into routine assessment for seniors. Summaries were sent to physicians and patients in the experimental condition; controls received usual care. Direct comparison of PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals and patients versus no feedback on processes of care (medication prescribing) and patient-reported pain.

The abstract provided does not match the title and describes a psychometric validation study of a self-care screening tool for the general population during COVID-19 lockdown. It is not an RCT comparing PROMs feedback to healthcare providers or patients versus no feedback.

RCT in primary healthcare where patients completed the Work Stress Questionnaire (PROM) and physicians received feedback versus treatment as usual. Direct comparison of PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback on healthcare use and treatment outcomes.

RCT comparing monthly telephone monitoring of distress using PROMs plus educational materials versus educational materials alone. The intervention is care management and referral triggered by cutoff scores rather than routine feedback of PROMs results to healthcare providers and patients. Actual scores are not fed back; only binary referral alerts are triggered.

Multisite RCT in psychiatric clinics randomly assigning patients to the OQ-Analyst feedback system using the Outcome Questionnaire-45.2 (a PROM) versus no feedback. Direct comparison of PROMs feedback to healthcare providers (therapists) versus no feedback on clinical outcomes.

Pilot RCT of a mobile application for weekly symptom reporting (ESAS) with automated information cards and service recommendations. It is a digital health/self-management navigation tool rather than routine provision of PROMs feedback to healthcare providers and/or patients in clinical practice.

Cross-sectional mixed-methods study randomizing participants to evaluate graphic data-presentation formats. Not an RCT of clinical outcomes and does not compare provision versus non-provision of PROMs feedback in practice.

RCT of a preoperative knowledge-test feedback session versus routine education. The feedback is based on a knowledge test, not on patient-reported health outcome measurements (PROMs), and thus does not meet the review's intervention definition.

Qualitative interview study exploring GP opinions on routine depression severity questionnaires. Not an RCT and does not compare PROMs feedback versus no feedback on patient outcomes or processes of care.

Cluster RCT of a stroke self-management programme integrated into rehabilitation. The intervention focuses on self-efficacy and a patient-held workbook; no PROMs feedback to healthcare providers or patients is described.

RCT in an emergency department where patients completed the PRIME-MD (a psychiatric screening PROM). Patients were randomized to have results told to both patient and physician, to patient only, or to neither. This provides a direct comparison of PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals and/or patients versus no feedback on referral processes.

Design and methods paper describing a pragmatic cluster RCT protocol. The abstract states 'We plan to compare,' indicating no trial results are reported. Protocols without outcome data are not eligible.

RCT in oncology randomly assigning patients to usual care, HRQL assessment only, or HRQL assessment followed by structured interview and discussion with the treating nurse (feedback). The comparison between the feedback arm and usual care directly tests the effect of providing PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus not providing it on patient-reported outcomes and satisfaction.

RCT in cancer patients where self-reported needs, QOL and psychosocial information (PROMs) collected via standardized questionnaires were made available to the healthcare team for two-thirds of patients (intervention) and withheld for one-third (control). Direct comparison of PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback on patient-reported outcomes and psychosocial functioning.
Protocol for a pragmatic RCT. No results are reported; only the study design and planned methods are described. As a protocol, it does not provide outcome data for inclusion in the review.

This trial evaluates a fully automated Internet-based self-monitoring and self-help programme (Featback) for eating disorders. The intervention is a digital therapeutic, not the routine provision of PROM feedback to healthcare providers to guide clinical care. The therapist support arms involve counselling, not PROM-based feedback.
This is a scoping review and commentary on quality of care frameworks for multimorbidity. It is not a randomised trial and does not evaluate PROM feedback.

Randomised controlled trial in which patient-reported outcome data from telephone interviews were fed back to either a telephone caseworker or the oncologist/GP, compared with usual care. This directly compares PROM feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback on patient-reported health outcomes and processes of care.
Methodological article on statistical heterogeneity in meta-analyses. Not a randomised trial of PROM feedback.

Randomised trial comparing QoL questionnaire completion with feedback during clinic versus questionnaire completion without feedback versus no questionnaire. This includes a direct comparison of PROM feedback versus no feedback in a clinical practice setting, with outcomes including QoL issues identified and actions taken.

Randomised trial in which ambulatory care patients were screened with the Zung self-rating depression scale and results were fed back to physicians in some groups. This represents an RCT of patient-reported depression scale feedback to physicians versus no such feedback, examining detection and management outcomes.
Qualitative interview study exploring oncologists' views on QoL information. Not a randomised trial.
This is a meta-analysis and theoretical review of feedback interventions in general. It is not a primary randomised trial of PROM feedback in clinical practice.

Randomised trial in which computer-generated health status reports (AIMS/MHAQ) were provided to physicians for patients with rheumatoid arthritis versus attention placebo and control. This directly compares PROM feedback to healthcare providers versus no feedback.

Randomised controlled trial in which a summary of patient-completed pain scales was placed in the clinical chart for oncologists to review before the visit, compared with no summary available. This is direct feedback of patient-reported pain outcomes to physicians versus no feedback.
Study describing the development and preliminary validation of the EMPRO tool for assessing PRO instruments. Not a trial of PROM feedback to providers or patients.
Cluster RCT evaluating brief telephone tobacco cessation counselling by pharmacists. The intervention is counselling, not feedback of patient-reported outcome measurements to clinicians or patients.
Review and conceptual article discussing different applications of PROs in clinical practice. Not a primary randomised trial.

Pilot RCT in which hematopoietic stem cell transplantation inpatients reported symptoms daily via electronic PROs (PRO-CTCAE) to nurses in the transplant clinic, compared with usual care. This is PROM feedback to nursing staff during inpatient clinical care.

Randomised trial in which postoperative cancer patients reported symptoms via automated telephone calls and email alerts were sent to the clinical team when severity thresholds were reached, compared with no alerts. This is PROM feedback to clinicians with action thresholds versus no feedback.

Randomised trial in which General Health Questionnaire (GHQ) results were fed back to primary care clinicians for randomly allocated patients versus no feedback. This directly compares PROM feedback to physicians with no feedback, examining detection and management outcomes.

This RCT randomised patients to one of two active intervention arms (nurse-led comorbidity reporting to physicians versus patient self-assessment of disease activity shared with rheumatologists). There is no control arm without feedback of patient-reported information, so it does not directly compare PROM feedback versus no feedback.

Randomised trial comparing routine OQ-45 feedback to clinicians (and patients at risk) versus no feedback in psychiatric outpatients. This is a direct comparison of PROM feedback versus no feedback on treatment outcomes.

Multicentre phase III RCT comparing web-mediated follow-up based on weekly self-scored patient symptoms with automatic email alerts to oncologists versus routine scheduled follow-up with CT scans. This compares PROM-based symptom monitoring and feedback to clinicians versus standard care without such feedback.
Study describing the development and Rasch validation of a disease-specific fatigue measure for motor neurone disease. Not a trial of PROM feedback.

Pilot RCT of feedback based on personality inventory (NEO PI-R) results to patients in residential substance use treatment. Personality testing is not a patient-reported health outcome measure in the sense of the review, and the intervention is a therapeutic assessment approach rather than routine PROM feedback to healthcare providers to guide care.
Discussion and commentary paper on the broader use of PROs. Not a primary randomised trial.

Prospective randomised crossover trial in which patients completed an HRQL questionnaire and computer-generated graphic summaries were provided to physicians and patients before the consultation, compared with no such assessment/feedback. This directly compares PROM feedback to both clinicians and patients versus no feedback, with communication and awareness outcomes.

Randomised clinical trial in which PROMIS symptom scores were displayed to primary care clinicians before the visit versus not provided. This is a direct comparison of PROM feedback to clinicians versus no feedback on symptom outcomes and processes of care.

Randomised trial with three arms: standard psychiatric assessment, QoL assessment plus standard, and QoL feedback to clinicians plus standard. This includes a direct comparison of PROM feedback to clinicians versus no feedback, with patient satisfaction and clinical outcomes assessed.

Multicentre pilot RCT in which children or parents completed PRO surveys and printed reports were provided to oncologists and families, with email alerts for high scores, versus no feedback. This directly compares PROM feedback to providers and families with no feedback on symptom distress and HRQoL.

RCT comparing use of parent-completed developmental screening tools at a single well-baby visit with usual care. This is a one-time screening intervention rather than the routine provision of PROM feedback on health outcomes during ongoing clinical care, and the tools are screening instruments rather than health outcome measures.

Pragmatic RCT comparing a novel care pathway involving QoL profile assessment, expert report generation, and feedback to the coordinating practitioner who arranged tailored QoL therapy, versus standard postoperative care. This is PROM feedback to healthcare providers driving management decisions versus no feedback.

This is a commentary by a scientific advisory board on a quality monitoring project, not a primary report of an RCT. Moreover, the intervention appears to be a system-level quality assurance procedure rather than routine PROM feedback to individual clinicians during patient care.

Randomised trial in which patients completed the electronic Lung Cancer Symptom Scale and real-time data were provided to oncologists before clinic visits versus standard clinical assessment alone. This directly compares PROM feedback to clinicians versus no feedback on supportive care referral and HRQoL outcomes.

Prospective controlled study (RCT design) in which emergency physicians were provided with patient GHQ scores before evaluation versus no feedback. This compares patient-reported psychiatric screening feedback to physicians versus no feedback, examining detection and referral outcomes.

Randomised controlled trial in which Beck Depression Inventory scores for previously undetected depression were disclosed to general practitioners versus not disclosed. This is direct feedback of patient-reported depression outcomes to primary care physicians versus no feedback, with depression status outcomes.

Randomised controlled trial in which patient-reported symptoms and quality-of-life issues were automatically displayed on a graphical summary provided to the clinical team before an on-treatment visit, versus no summary. This directly compares electronic PROM feedback to clinicians versus no feedback on communication outcomes.

Randomised controlled trial comparing a flare-management intervention guided by monthly FLARE-RA questionnaire (a patient-reported outcome measure of flare status) versus usual care. The questionnaire results triggered telephone nurse-led counselling or expedited rheumatology visits, representing PROM feedback to providers with the aim of affecting disease activity and flare outcomes.
This is a commentary/opinion piece describing examples of PROM use and arguing for wider uptake. It is not a randomised trial and does not compare PROM feedback versus no feedback.
A review/framework paper discussing implementation of PROs in clinical settings. Not a randomised trial and contains no comparison of PROM feedback versus no feedback.

Randomised trial of a short-term life review psychological intervention versus usual care. The intervention does not involve feedback of patient-reported outcome measurement results to clinicians or patients.

Randomised trial of depression screening (PC-SAD) with feedback versus no feedback. Although the screener is patient-reported, this is a case-finding/screening program for early detection of depression rather than routine feedback of patient-reported outcome measurements to support ongoing clinical care, and thus falls outside the review scope.

Practice-randomised trial of depression care management (algorithm-based care, psychotherapy, medication management) versus usual care. The intervention is a care-management programme, not the provision of feedback from patient-reported outcome measurements.

Randomised trial directly comparing feedback of Adverse Event Profile (AEP) scores— a patient-reported measure of antiepileptic drug adverse effects—to treating physicians versus no feedback. Assesses patient-reported outcomes (AEP scores, QOLIE-31 quality of life).

Randomised trial comparing the Partners for Change Outcome Management System (PCOMS), a continuous patient-reported outcome feedback system, versus a no-feedback control in psychotherapy. Assesses treatment gains and reliable change in patient-reported outcomes.

Cluster randomised trial of a physical-activity monitoring and feedback tool plus self-management support versus support alone or usual care. The intervention monitors physical activity behaviour, not patient-reported health outcomes, and therefore does not meet the PROM feedback criterion.

Experimental study in healthy undergraduates without mild traumatic brain injury examining the effect of PCSQ screening feedback on symptom report and cognitive performance. Not conducted in a clinical practice setting and not a trial of PROM feedback for health-care decision-making.

Cluster randomised trial of electronic pre-visit questionnaire feedback on youth violence to primary-care physicians. The questionnaire assesses violence involvement (a health risk behaviour), not a patient-reported health outcome, and the focus is risk-behaviour screening rather than PROM feedback.

Randomised controlled trial comparing a QoL-monitor (assessing QoL, distress and care needs) with feedback of results to both patients and healthcare providers versus usual care. Assesses processes of care (communication score) and patient wellbeing/satisfaction.

Randomised trial of composite screening questionnaire disclosure to GPs versus blinding. This is a case-finding/screening study for common mental disorders rather than routine feedback of patient-reported outcome measurements for ongoing care.
Study developing a classification system for PRO measures based on conceptual models. Not a randomised trial and does not compare PROM feedback versus no feedback.

Cluster randomised trial providing physicians with alcohol screening results (CAGE, consumption, readiness to change) and recommendations. CAGE is a screening tool for alcohol misuse, not a patient-reported health outcome measure, and the focus is alcohol screening rather than PROM feedback.
This appears to be a systematic review (abstract references Cochrane Library) of routine PROM use in common mental health disorders. Not a primary randomised trial.

The abstract indicates a study on daily sun-protection feedback. It is not a randomised trial comparing feedback of patient-reported outcome measurements to clinicians/patients versus no feedback on health outcomes or processes of care.

Pilot cluster randomised trial of a web-based team communication tool (Loop) versus usual care. The intervention is a collaborative communication platform, not the routine feedback of patient-reported outcome measurement results.

Cluster randomised controlled trial directly comparing peer-benchmarked patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) feedback to surgeons versus no feedback. Assesses patient-reported outcomes postoperatively (Oxford Hip Score, HOOS, EQ-5D).

Randomised trial comparing feedback on patient progress (derived from ongoing patient-reported outcome monitoring) to therapists versus control conditions. Assesses patient outcome and number of sessions, fitting the scope of PROM feedback in clinical practice.

Randomised controlled trial comparing provision of self-administered computerized patient-reported mental health assessment (PROQSY) results to GPs versus no additional information or GHQ results only. Assesses clinical outcome (GHQ) and health-service use.

Randomised trial comparing systematic HRQOL (KIDSCREEN-27) monitoring with face-to-face discussion of results between pediatrician and patient versus usual care. Directly assesses effects on patient-reported HRQOL outcomes.

Pragmatic cluster randomised trial of the STarT Back risk-stratification strategy (training clinicians to use a patient-reported tool and match treatments) versus control. This is a complex implementation intervention for stratified care, not a direct comparison of PROM feedback alone versus no feedback.

Preliminary randomised trial of a recovery-focused package (wellbeing assessment, counselling, diagnostic consultation with written feedback, post-diagnostic support) versus treatment as usual. The intervention is a multi-component psychiatric package, not a direct test of PROM feedback versus no feedback.
Guidance paper from the Medical Research Council on evaluating complex interventions. Not a randomised trial.

Randomised trial comparing in-person alcohol counselling versus computer-generated feedback letters versus assessment only in hospital inpatients. The feedback is based on at-risk alcohol use screening, not patient-reported health outcome measurements, and the setting is not routine clinical practice for health outcomes.

Randomised trial protocol comparing modes of PROM administration (telephone, postal, online versus face-to-face). The study compares methods of collecting PROM data, not the effects of feeding PROM results back to clinicians or patients versus no feedback.

Randomised controlled trial directly comparing SF-36 health survey results given to physicians before the patient encounter versus results withheld (usual care). Assesses processes of care (physician-reported usefulness, change in therapy) and patient satisfaction.

Randomised clinical trial of electronic screening for health risk behaviours with personalised feedback and clinical decision support. The intervention addresses health risk behaviours, not patient-reported health outcomes, and is therefore outside the review scope.
Realist synthesis examining how PROMs support communication and care. Not a primary randomised trial and does not directly compare PROM feedback versus no feedback.

Randomised trial directly comparing feedback of patient-reported symptoms and preferences (collected via tablet and provided to patient and clinician in consultation) versus no feedback. Assesses congruence between reported and addressed symptoms (process of care).

Randomised trial directly comparing use of the Adverse Events Profile (AEP)—a patient-reported measure of antiepileptic drug adverse effects—fed back to clinicians versus usual care without the AEP. Assesses adverse effects and Quality of Life in Epilepsy Inventory (QOLIE-89) outcomes.

RCT of mobile-phone home telehealth in diabetes with nurse-initiated feedback of self-monitoring data; the intervention centres on telehealth transmission of clinical/behavioural data rather than feedback of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) to providers or patients about health outcomes.

RCT comparing treatment as usual with therapist feedback and patient-therapist feedback in outpatient psychotherapy; directly evaluates feedback of patient progress/outcomes (patient-reported) to therapists and/or patients versus no feedback.
Study describing the development and preliminary psychometric testing of a haemophilia-specific quality-of-life questionnaire; no RCT comparing PROM feedback versus no feedback.

Multicenter cluster-randomised phase III trial in which patients complete patient-reported symptom assessments and oncologists receive a longitudinal monitoring sheet (LoMoS) print-out versus usual care; compares PROM feedback to healthcare providers with no feedback.

Group-randomised trial of a symptom assessment and management intervention (SAMI) that provides tailored longitudinal symptom reports and management suggestions to clinicians based on web-based patient assessments; compares PROM feedback to clinicians versus usual care.

Prospective randomised quality-improvement initiative providing real-time patient experience/satisfaction surveys to physicians; patient experience is distinct from patient-reported health outcomes (PROMs), and the feedback is about care perceptions rather than health status.

Study examining whether giving physicians depression screening results alters chart notation; not a randomised trial comparing PROM feedback versus no feedback on patient outcomes or processes of care.
Cochrane review of health-service or patient-oriented interventions for multimorbidity; this is a systematic review, not a primary randomised trial of PROM feedback.

RCT comparing control, feedback, and feedback/protocol clinics; provides detailed feedback about patients’ mental health problems and intervention desires to physicians, comparing PROM-based feedback versus no feedback on counselling outcomes.

RCT of technology-assisted symptom monitoring plus feedback versus usual care in prostate cancer survivors; compares feedback of patient-reported symptoms and HRQOL to providers/patients with no feedback.
RCT of computer-generated feedback to physicians about patients’ functional status and management suggestions versus usual care; directly compares PROM feedback to physicians with no feedback.

RCT of outcome monitoring feedback to therapists and/or patients versus no feedback in short- and long-term psychotherapy; uses progress charts based on the Outcome Questionnaire to compare PROM feedback conditions with none.
RCT of routine monthly postal standardised outcome measures with 3-monthly feedback versus treatment as usual in adult mental health services; compares routine PROM feedback versus no feedback.

RCT evaluating the addition of personalised feedback to guided CBT self-help for bulimia nervosa; delivers feedback on physical/psychological status to patients, comparing added PROM patient feedback versus no added feedback.

RCT of a systematic symptom monitoring instrument versus no monitor in palliative cancer; the intervention is patient symptom reporting alone without clear evidence that PROM data were fed back to healthcare providers or patients to guide clinical care.

RCT of patient-reported symptom monitoring via tablet computers with symptom printouts given to treating physicians and e-mail alerts to nurses versus usual care; compares PROM feedback to providers versus no feedback.
RCT of outcome monitoring feedback to therapists versus no-feedback control in clinical practice; examines the effect of PROM feedback on treatment outcomes.

RCT of a video decision aid versus standard educational materials for lung cancer screening decisions; intervention is decision support for screening, not feedback of patient-reported health outcomes to providers or patients during clinical care.

RCT of a two-stage emergency department screening and nursing assessment intervention with disclosure of ISAR screen results; ISAR is a geriatric risk screening tool, not a patient-reported outcome measure for health status feedback.

RCT of an electronic PRO-tool for adverse event reporting by melanoma patients versus standard clinician monitoring; no clear evidence that patient-reported data were fed back to healthcare providers to guide management, and the study focuses on detection rather than feedback.

Pilot RCT of an electronic symptom monitoring intervention in which patient symptom reports are presented graphically with alerts during daily team rounds versus usual care; compares PROM feedback to providers versus no feedback.

Noninferiority RCT comparing smartphone app-based remote symptom and biomarker monitoring versus standard face-to-face outpatient care in inflammatory bowel disease; the intervention is a broader telemedicine care delivery model rather than solely routine PROM feedback to providers/patients.

RCT of access to an e-health interactive self-assessment platform (Sanoia) versus usual care in rheumatoid arthritis; the intervention is patient self-assessment/self-monitoring without explicit feedback of PROMs to healthcare providers to guide care.

Three-armed RCT of ecological momentary assessment with texting feedback during drinking events to reduce alcohol use; this is a real-time behavioural intervention targeting alcohol consumption, not routine feedback of patient-reported health outcomes to healthcare providers in clinical practice.

Cluster-randomised trial of outcome management with weekly computerised standardised assessments and continuous feedback of outcomes to patients and clinicians versus no feedback in inpatient psychiatric care; compares PROM feedback to both versus none.

RCT in which intervention physicians were provided with Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) scores and treatment recommendations; HAM-D is a clinician-rated scale, not a patient-reported outcome measure, so it does not meet the PROM requirement.

RCT of a postoperative web-based app providing real-time symptom monitoring with patient self-reported health information integrated into electronic health records and alerts versus usual care; compares PROM feedback to providers via EHR versus no feedback.

Pilot study of an automated interactive voice response intervention for symptom monitoring with e-mail alerts to oncologists for moderate-to-severe symptoms versus control; compares PROM feedback to providers versus usual care.
Study describing the development and psychometric validation of the ADDQoL questionnaire for diabetes; no RCT comparing PROM feedback versus no feedback.

Cluster-randomised trial comparing feedback of End-of-Life in Dementia scores versus no feedback; however, the instruments were completed by bereaved family caregivers (proxy-reported), not by the patients themselves, so it does not meet the patient-reported outcome requirement.
Descriptive article summarising the NIH PROMIS Roadmap cooperative group and item bank development during its first two years; not a primary RCT evaluating the effects of PROM feedback.

RCT comparing nurse-led telephone follow-up versus traditional hospital follow-up for stage-I endometrial cancer; the intervention is a follow-up delivery modality rather than feedback of patient-reported outcome measures to providers or patients.

Randomised controlled trial comparing physician-targeted feedback of patient-specific treatment recommendations (derived in part from a patient-reported depression scale) versus usual care, measuring processes of care (diagnosis, prescribing) and patient outcomes (HAM-D, SIP). Meets the criterion of a randomised trial directly comparing PROMs-based feedback to healthcare professionals with no feedback.

Randomised clinical trial in oncology in which patient self-reported symptom summaries were provided to physicians and nurses in the intervention group but not the control group. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers versus no feedback, assessing patient-reported outcomes and processes of care.

Randomised controlled trial comparing experience-sampling self-monitoring with weekly feedback sessions to patients versus treatment as usual, measuring empowerment. Involves feedback of patient-reported data to patients in a clinical practice population.

Randomised trial comparing Nintendo Wii virtual rehabilitation with conventional physical therapy. The feedback mentioned is device-driven motor performance feedback during gameplay, not feedback of patient-reported outcome measures to healthcare providers or patients.

Randomised clinical trial comparing provision of treatment progress and alliance information (patient-reported feedback) to both clients and therapists during couple therapy versus treatment as usual. Directly tests PROMs feedback to patients and healthcare providers.

Study describes the development and validation of the Dartmouth COOP Charts and tests their reliability and utility; it is not a randomised trial comparing the effects of PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

Randomised controlled trial comparing provision of PROMIS Pain Interference feedback to patients prior to consultation versus no feedback, measuring satisfaction and communication. Directly tests patient-facing PROMs feedback against no feedback.

Abstract describes a feedback-plus-clinical-support-tools intervention versus treatment as usual but does not explicitly state that participants were randomly assigned. The review inclusion criteria require randomised trials.
This is a systematic review of randomised clinical trials, not a primary randomised trial itself.

Cluster randomised controlled trial comparing feedback of patient-reported asthma information to primary care teams versus no feedback, measuring symptoms, health service use and medication use. Directly tests PRO feedback to healthcare professionals.
Commentary article discussing NHS policy on patient-reported outcomes; not a randomised trial.

Randomised controlled trial comparing provision of patient-completed PRIME-MD diagnostic results to emergency physicians versus no report, measuring psychiatric diagnosis and referral. Directly tests patient-reported feedback to clinicians.
Study evaluates the Sickness Impact Profile instrument with physicians and patients; it is not a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

Study compares clinicians using COOP Charts with control clinicians not using them, but the abstract does not explicitly report randomisation; therefore it cannot be confirmed as meeting the randomised trial criterion based on title and abstract alone.

Randomised trial compares two active mHealth interventions: both arms collect patient-reported data and provide feedback to the clinical team (fax alerts). The intervention arm additionally emails feedback to a caregiver. Because both arms provide PROMs-based feedback to clinicians, it does not directly compare PROMs feedback with no feedback.
Randomised trial of stellate ganglion block versus sham for PTSD; no patient-reported outcome feedback intervention is tested.

Feasibility randomised trial comparing PROMs monitoring for depression with feedback of scores to patients/practitioners versus control, measuring depression, functioning and quality-of-life outcomes. Directly tests PROMs feedback.

Randomised trial comparing clinicians receiving patient-reported mental health assessment feedback versus no report in a managed behavioural healthcare setting, measuring clinical status. Directly tests PRO feedback to clinicians.

Cluster randomised controlled trial of a DIALOG intervention where patient-reported quality-of-life and needs ratings are fed back immediately to clinicians and discussed versus treatment as usual. Directly tests structured PRO feedback to clinicians.
Abstract describes an observational study of HRQoL in a weight-management sample without a randomised comparison of PROMs feedback versus no feedback. Not a relevant primary trial.

Randomised clinical trial testing feedback of General Health Questionnaire screening results to primary care clinicians versus no feedback, measuring detection and management of mental health problems. Directly tests PRO feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomised trial comparing provision of patient progress information and clinical support tools to both patients and therapists versus treatment as usual, measuring psychotherapy outcomes. Directly tests patient-reported feedback to both patients and providers.

Randomised controlled study comparing use of a depression self-rating scale (MADRS) in GP consultations with feedback and discussion versus treatment as usual. Directly tests PRO feedback to clinicians.
Systematic review of feedback interventions; not a primary randomised trial.

Randomised controlled trial comparing physical function assessment with feedback to the patient and physician versus assessment alone, measuring health status outcomes. Directly tests functional-status feedback to patients and providers.
Review article summarising considerations for implementing PRO assessment in practice; not a primary randomised trial.
Qualitative study of GP views on using mental health questionnaires; not a randomised trial.
Study protocol for web-based CBT in chronic fatigue syndrome; the intervention is cognitive behavioural therapy, not feedback of PROMs versus no feedback.
Bibliographic study mapping the development of patient-assessed outcome measures; not a randomised trial.

Randomised trial in paediatric dentistry where both study and control groups handed a report to the dentist; it does not compare PROMs feedback with no feedback, and the control also received a minimal report.

Randomised controlled trial comparing monitoring and discussion of psychological well-being using a patient-reported questionnaire versus standard care in diabetes outpatients, measuring mood and care evaluation. Directly tests PRO feedback to patients and nurses.
Commentary/discussion article on moving PROs into clinical practice; not a randomised trial.

This RCT tests optimized tailored feedback messages for an online health risk assessment in a general population sample recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk. The intervention provides automated health behavior feedback directly to participants, not to healthcare providers in a clinical practice setting. It does not examine PROMs feedback to clinicians or patients in routine care.
This is a small qualitative interview study of health visitors. It is not a randomized trial and does not compare PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

Randomized trial in rural primary care comparing depression screening using the PHQ-9 (a patient-reported outcome measure) with feedback of completed questionnaires to providers versus no feedback. Directly assesses effects on management and outcomes, meeting the review's selection criteria.

This is a validation and psychometric study of a hearing self-assessment questionnaire against audiometric evaluation. It is not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to clinicians versus no feedback.

Laboratory experiment examining acute effects of heart-rate feedback on self-reported stress. The feedback is physiological, not a patient-reported outcome measure provided to healthcare professionals or patients in clinical practice.

Cluster RCT of structured discharge readiness protocols. Although it includes a patient self-assessment scale, the intervention is a complex discharge readiness protocol rather than routine feedback of PROMs to providers/patients for care improvement.

RCT of a web-based self-care and communication coaching intervention. Clinicians in both intervention and control groups received summaries of participant reports, so the comparison is not specifically PROMs feedback versus no feedback; rather it adds self-care instruction and coaching.

Abstract does not describe a randomized trial design; it appears to be a study of screening impact on resident recognition of depression without a clear randomized comparison of PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

Randomized trial comparing weekly OQ-45 patient progress feedback (a patient-reported outcome measure) provided to therapists versus treatment as usual without such feedback. Directly assesses effects on patient outcomes for at-risk inpatients.
This is a literature review of thirteen studies from 1987-97, not a primary randomized trial.

RCT evaluating a mobile app for syndromic disease surveillance in a low-resource setting. The purpose is surveillance and pathogen detection, not feedback of PROMs to healthcare providers or patients to improve clinical care processes or outcomes.

Randomized controlled trial in lung-transplant outpatients comparing HRQL (HUI2/HUI3) assessment with graphical feedback to clinicians versus assessment without feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback versus no feedback on communication, management, and outcomes.

Pilot RCT of a comprehensive web-based asthma self-management portal coupled with nurse case management. The intervention includes multiple components (self-monitoring, coaching, support) and is not a direct comparison of PROMs feedback alone versus no feedback.

Randomized trial comparing routine online distress screening (Distress Thermometer, problem checklist, Psychological Screen for Cancer) with a personalized report placed on the medical file versus minimal screening without provider feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback on patient distress outcomes.
PLoS Medicine Debate article discussing methodological challenges in reviewing complex interventions. Not a primary randomized trial.
RCT of a communication skills training program for oncologists. The intervention targets clinician communication skills, not feedback of patient-reported outcome measures to providers or patients.

Cluster randomized trial in elderly primary care patients comparing case-finding with the Geriatric Depression Scale (a patient-reported outcome measure) and feedback of scores to physicians versus usual care without feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback versus no feedback on diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes.

Randomized trial comparing disclosure of Beck Depression Inventory (a patient-reported outcome measure) scores to general practitioners versus no disclosure. Directly assesses effects on diagnosis and management, matching the review's selection criteria.

Cluster RCT of a bilateral communication-priming intervention (Jumpstart-Tips) to increase goals-of-care discussions. The intervention is about communication priming, not feedback of patient-reported outcome measures.
Opinion piece/editorial discussing the potential of PROMs to transform healthcare. Not a randomized trial.
Study design and recruitment report for the COmPASS II study. It describes app-based self-monitoring setup but does not report outcomes of a randomized comparison; it is a protocol/recruitment paper.

Cluster RCT of tailored printouts about colorectal cancer risk and screening generated by a computer program. The intervention provides tailored risk information, not feedback of patient-reported outcome measures.
RCT evaluating structured nurse telephone follow-up after knee surgery. The intervention is post-discharge telephone follow-up, not feedback of PROMs to clinicians or patients.
Systematic review of randomized trials of psychiatric questionnaire feedback. Not a primary randomized trial itself.
Methodological article about the GRADE system for rating evidence. Not a clinical trial.
Conceptual review article defining comorbidity and related constructs. Not a randomized trial.

RCT comparing a web-based survivorship care system with remote nurse practitioner review of online symptom questionnaires versus standard care. The intervention is a comprehensive follow-up care delivery model, not a direct comparison of routine PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

Single-blind RCT (FOCUS) investigating routine completion and feedback of standardized outcome measures versus control in adult mental health services. Directly compares routine PROMs feedback versus no feedback and assesses effects on patient outcomes.

Prospective RCT in chronic liver disease outpatients comparing computerized HRQoL measurement with instant online graphical feedback to physicians versus measurement without feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback versus no feedback on HRQoL outcomes and patient management.
Overview of existing phase III trials in prostate cancer examining how HRQoL was reported as an endpoint. Not a primary randomized trial of PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

Cluster RCT of a multifaceted tailored implementation intervention (outreach visits, website, tools, CME) to improve adherence to depression guidelines. The intervention targets guideline implementation, not feedback of patient-reported outcome measures.
Product description for EndNote reference management software. Not a clinical study.
